change_summary: PLOS ONE editors retracted the article. The retraction is because the article was one of a series of submissions with concerns about peer review integrity and potential manipulation of the publication process. These concerns call into question the validity and provenance of the reported results. The author either did not respond directly or could not be reached.
evaluation: Your Section 3 cites Dutta [14] as the main evidence for choosing an LSTM, quoting LURL's 97.4% and 96.8% accuracies, which the stored paper reports. Your Section 4 starts from the LURL settings reported by Dutta [14], and the stored paper's Table 2 lists them, including a hidden size of 650. PLOS ONE editors retracted the article, and the notice says the concerns call into question the validity and provenance of the reported results. Both uses are touched, because your detector choice and your starting settings rest on the retracted paper's results; this matters a great deal for the draft.
recommendation: PLOS ONE editors retracted the article, and the notice says the concerns call into question the validity and provenance of the reported results. Your Section 3 cites Dutta [14] as the main evidence for choosing an LSTM, quoting LURL's accuracy of 97.4% on Phishtank and 96.8% on Crawler. Your Section 4 starts from the LURL settings reported by Dutta [14], including two LSTM layers and a hidden size of 650. Raise this with your co-authors or supervisor before going further, replace the evidence for the detector choice, and set your starting configuration independently.
